Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for acute left-sided headache that woke patient from sleep; GP impression tension-type vs migraine; advised ibuprofen and supportive measures; 1-week follow-up planned.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe left-sided headache starting early this morning (~05:30), woke patient from sleep; still present; paracetamol taken with no relief.
- Associated symptoms: Mild photophobia; transient dizziness on waking (resolved); no nausea; no fever; no neck stiffness. Initially more sore when lying down, then improves; overall better when lying down.
- Headache history: Prior headaches milder, usually frontal “cluster,” not typically one-sided. No family history of migraine.
- Psychosocial: Work stress for ~2 months with late nights. Mood variable; denies significant ongoing anxiety outside work-related stress. Denies suicidal ideation/self-harm thoughts.
- Past medical history: Anxiety (≈2 years).
- Family history: Mother with anxiety; otherwise negative per patient.
- Medications: 
  - Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Paracetamol taken today for headache (dose/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Social history: Lives with partner; non-smoker; runs ~3x/week; diet “okay;” has a cat. No blood pressure checks previously.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not performed (telehealth; no direct exam documented).

Impression:
- Acute unilateral headache, working diagnosis: migraine vs tension-type headache. Unilateral pain and photophobia support migraine; work-related stress and anxiety history support tension-type. No red-flag features elicited in history.

Plan:
- Analgesia: Start ibuprofen as first-line for suspected migraine (dose/route/frequency not documented). May continue paracetamol if desired.
- Stress management: Consider taking ~1 week off work (self-certify). GP to provide link for local counseling service for self-referral.
- Lifestyle: Aim for 7–8 hours sleep nightly; hydrate 1.5–2.0 L fluids/day (excluding coffee/tea). Recognize dehydration and fatigue as potential headache contributors.
- Follow-up: GP review in 1 week. If not improving, consider blood tests and further evaluation.
- Safety-net: Read provided information on headache danger signs; seek earlier care if symptoms worsen or new symptoms develop.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - No vitals or in-person neurologic exam.
  - No blood pressure measurement.
  - No documentation of visual changes, focal neurologic deficits, head trauma, thunderclap onset, jaw/temporal symptoms, or other red-flag screening beyond fever/neck stiffness/photophobia/nausea.
  - Ibuprofen dosing and contraindication screening (e.g., GI/renal/cardiovascular risk, anticoagulants) not documented.
  - Sertraline dose and full medication reconciliation not documented.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Patient’s name referenced variably: introduced as “Atan,” stated as “Ayrton Warren,” and addressed by clinician as “Anthony” (conflict noted).
● Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; minor pauses/incomplete phrases but clinically adequate.
